To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

co-inactivation (in a single mutant) of GlnR (regulator of glutamine/glutarate metabolism) and CodY (nutritional regulator) impact pneumococcal physiology, and that this is manifested in the form of altered ultrastructure of cell wall, and hypersensitivity of the mutant to iron and peptidogycan targeting agents.

co-inactivation (i.e., double knockout) of two regulators, GlnR (glutamine regulator) and CodY (nutritional regulator), impacts pneumocococcal cell-wall physiology, and that co-inactivation renders pneumococcal cells sensitive to peptidoylcan (PG)-targeting agents, such as antibiotics and lysozyme, and to iron.
co-inactivation (i.e., simultaneous inactivation) of the GlnR and the CodY regulators in the pneumococcus impacts pneumococci cell wall physiology.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the mechanisms by which pneumococci survive in the absence of CodY.
the role of the nutritional regulator CodY and its interplay with other regulators in the pathogen pneumococcus.
the identification and analysis of new regulators of pneumococcal physiology, and the elucidation of the role of these regulators in pneumococcal pathogenesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the CodY regulator in S. pneumoniae is essential and that the primary suppressors of codY inactivation are inactivation of fatC or fecE, which are both involved in iron import, while secondary suppressors are inactivation of amiC, which is involved in oligopeptide import.
CodY regulates competence indirectly via Ami, and that co-inactivation with GlnR impacts pneumococci cell wall physiology.

CodY is essential in the pneumococcus and that the primary function of CodY is to repress fat/fec operons, which is required to ensure survival without CodY, while the secondary function is to indirectly activate competence.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CodY is essential for pneumococci, and that the essentiality of this nutritional regulator is linked to iron import and cell wall physiology.
CodY is a global regulator of pneumococcal physiology, and its absence results in a pleiotropic phenotype that is not fully understood.

the GlnR/CodY regulatory network impacts pneumococci in two ways: (1) by repressing iron uptake, the network contributes to pneumococcal virulence by limiting iron availability to host cells; and (2) by represssing ami, the network contributes indirectly to the regulation of competence for genetic transformation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
co-inactivation or inhibition of GlnR or CodY in S. pneumoniae can render pneumococci susceptible to PG-targeting drugs.
